name: Dharam Pal Gulati
profile: Founder/owner and face of MDH spices; died 3 December 2020 in New Delhi aged 97 (post-COVID cardiac arrest).
notes: Deceased 3 Dec 2020 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharampal_Gulati, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/owner-of-mdh-masala-dies-at-97-179362). Business now run by son Rajiv Gulati.

name: Hu Zuliu
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Primavera Capital Group; non-executive chairman, Yum China
profile: Fred Hu Zuliu is a Harvard-trained economist who worked at the IMF, then became Goldman Sachs' Partner and Chairman of Greater China. In 2010 he founded Primavera Capital, an Asia growth-equity firm that backed Alibaba, Ant Group, ByteDance, Kuaishou, Xpeng and Yum China; he still runs it and chairs its investment committee.
interesting_fact: Primavera initiated or led investments in Alibaba, Cainiao, Ant Group, Yum China, ByteDance, Xpeng, Kuaishou and SenseTime; Hu also sits on the boards of UBS Group and ICBC.
deep_cut_fact: Before economics he trained as an engineer, earning a Master in Engineering Science at Tsinghua before his Harvard PhD; he is also a trustee of Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study and co-chairs The Nature Conservancy's Asia Pacific Council.
notes: Frequent speaker at WEF, Milken and HKU AsiaGlobal events; conference circuit is a natural route. Writes WEF agenda pieces.

name: Rachael A. Wagner
current_role: Partner, Atairos Management (leisure, entertainment & digital media); director, Life Time Group Holdings and Lucky Strike Entertainment
profile: Private-equity investor and Partner at Atairos, the Comcast-backed independent investment firm, where she leads leisure, entertainment and digital-media deals. She joined Atairos in 2016 from Lindsay Goldberg (MD 2012-16). She sits on the boards of Lucky Strike Entertainment (ex-Bowlero) since 2021 and Life Time since May 2026.
interesting_fact: She represents Atairos on the board of Lucky Strike (formerly Bowlero), the largest bowling-centre operator, where Atairos is a 10%+ holder - the source of her SEC 'TenPercentOwner' flag.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lindsay Goldberg she worked at consumer-focused buyout firm Lion Capital and in Blackstone's private equity group.
notes: Likely not personally UHNW: the 10%-owner SEC flag reflects Atairos' fund stake in Lucky Strike, not personal wealth. Low public profile.

name: Lord Iliffe
current_role: Chairman, Yattendon Group Plc (Iliffe family holding company)
profile: Robert Peter Richard Iliffe, 3rd Baron Iliffe (b. 1944), succeeded his uncle in 1996 and chairs the family-owned Yattendon Group. The family fortune began with his grandfather's Birmingham and Coventry newspapers; Yattendon today runs 19 marinas in the UK and Spain (MDL Marinas), newspaper printing, commercial property and a 9,000-acre West Berkshire estate. His son Edward is Group CEO.
interesting_fact: Yattendon's MDL Marinas describes itself as Europe's leading marina group with 19 marinas in the UK and Spain; the group also owns a craft brewery on its Berkshire estate.
deep_cut_fact: A keen yachtsman, Lord Iliffe has served as Commodore of the Royal Yacht Squadron at Cowes - fitting for a family business that became Europe's largest marina operator. The surname is pronounced 'EYE-liff'.
notes: Low-profile aristocratic family business; Commodore role date not confirmed as current. Son Edward Iliffe (Group CEO) is the operational lead and may be a better podcast guest.

name: Wu Changjiang
current_role: None known; former founder/chairman/CEO of NVC Lighting (removed from board 2014)
profile: Founder of NVC Lighting (雷士照明), established in late 1998 and listed in Hong Kong in 2010, once among China's largest lighting makers. After boardroom fights with investors he was voted off the board in August 2014 and was detained by Huizhou police in late 2014/early 2015 on suspected misappropriation of company funds. NVC sold 70% of its China business to KKR in 2019.
interesting_fact: NVC Lighting, founded in late 1998, sold 70% of its China lighting business to a KKR fund in 2019 for RMB 5.56bn.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: arrested 2014-15 on misappropriation charges (https://www.ledinside.com/news/2015/1/police_file_for_former_nvc_lighting_chairman_detainment); widely reported later conviction not verified here. No current role or public contact found.

name: Li Shiyong
current_role: Associated with Shandong Ensign Industry (formerly Weifang Ensign), Changle, Weifang; current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for wealth from Ensign, a citric-acid and alcohol producer. Shandong Ensign Industry (named Weifang Ensign until 2020) is reported to be the world's largest citric-acid producer, with ~600,000 t/a capacity and an upgrade planned to 700,000 t/a. Recent annual reports list Li Jian as company head; Li Shiyong's current role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Shandong Ensign has been described as the world's largest citric acid producer, planning to lift capacity from 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes a year.
interesting_fact_source: https://www.cnchemicals.com/Press/91863-Shandong Ensign: Citric acid capacity expansion proposal and refined citric acid project completion.html
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in English or Chinese web search, and Baidu Baike was not accessible. A 'Shiyong Li' appears as an inventor on Weifang Ensign patents (goodip.io). No published contact or company website found.

name: Ding Mingshan
current_role: Unknown (listed by Hurun China 2015-2019 as real-estate entrepreneur, company 'Wallink')
profile: Appears on the Hurun China Rich List (2015-2019) with real-estate wealth attributed to a company rendered 'Wallink'. Could not identify the company's Chinese name or confirm his current role from public web sources.
notes: Searches in English and Chinese (丁明山) returned no matching biography; Baidu Baike blocked. Identity unconfirmed - needs a Chinese registry check (e.g. 国家企业信用信息公示系统) to locate 'Wallink'.

name: Yang Xiaowei
current_role: Unknown; no current role at Jinfu Technology (300128) - its chairman is Gu Qing and control passed to a Taixing state body in 2019
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2013-2017) with wealth from Jinfu, matching Suzhou Jinfu Technology (formerly Suzhou Jinfu New Materials, Shenzhen ChiNext 300128), a maker of optical display films and precision die-cut parts. The company's actual controller changed in 2019 and is now a Taixing high-tech zone administration; Yang's present activities could not be confirmed.
notes: Linkage to Jinfu inferred from Hurun industry (electro-optic products) - not confirmed by a source naming Yang. Company has had regulatory issues post-2019 (under new control). Not a strong outreach target.

name: Shen Peijin
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Zhejiang Hugeleaf (浙江瀚叶股份); current role unknown
profile: Hugeleaf matches Zhejiang Hanye/Hugeleaf Co. (浙江瀚叶股份), where a CSRC Zhejiang 2021 penalty decision names 沈培今 (b. Feb 1979) as then chairman and actual controller. Hurun's spelling 沈培金 differs, so identity is likely but unconfirmed. Present role not found.
notes: Likely the 沈培今 named in a 2021 CSRC Zhejiang disclosure-violation penalty (https://www.csrc.gov.cn/zhejiang/c103940/c6d7fb00dcb7543db872e3b0c868bf931/content.shtml). Regulatory history makes him a poor outreach target.

name: Chen Yuemeng
current_role: Chairman and Founding Partner, Zheshang Venture Capital (ZSVC, 浙商创投, NEEQ 834089), Hangzhou
profile: Chen Yuemeng founded and chairs Zheshang Venture Capital, one of Zhejiang's leading private equity/VC managers, which has invested in about 100 projects with nearly 30 listed or acquired. He holds senior roles in Zhejiang's business community, including Standing Committee member of the Zhejiang CPPCC and first executive chairman of the Zhejiang Private Equity Association.
interesting_fact: Named one of Hurun China's Top 50 Best Venture Capitalists (2016) and Forbes China's Top 100 venture capital figures (2018); ZSVC has taken nearly 30 of ~100 portfolio companies to listing or M&A exit.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a VC, he graduated from Zhejiang University's Chinese language and literature department before taking an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.
notes: invest@ is the published project-submission mailbox (only email on the site); company also runs a WeChat official account. Active in Zhejiang chambers of commerce - possible intro route.

name: Yan Binsheng
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and controlling shareholder (~56%), Ganyuan Foods Co., Ltd. (甘源食品, SZSE 002991), Pingxiang, Jiangxi
profile: Yan Binsheng (b. 1975) built Ganyuan Foods, a Jiangxi-based snack maker known for green peas, sunflower kernels, broad beans and mixed nuts. After working at several Guangdong snack companies he joined Pingxiang Ganyuan as marketing director in 2006, became chairman in 2012 and chairman/GM in 2015; the company listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He holds about 56% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Ganyuan's core products are humble pantry snacks - green peas, sunflower seed kernels, broad beans and mixed nuts - sold nationally from a factory park in Pingxiang, Jiangxi.
deep_cut_fact: He came up through sales: before Ganyuan he worked at Guangdong Qibao Yiding Food and other Foshan/Shunde snack firms, and joined Pingxiang Ganyuan in 2006 as marketing director before rising to chairman in 2012.
notes: Board secretary is Zhang Ting (per 10jqka); IR email should be in the company's annual report on cninfo.com.cn (not verified here). Site lists only a sales/franchise mailbox. Snack-food founder - tangential to energy/data-centre themes.

name: Zhang Ji
current_role: Director and co-actual controller, Jiangsu Flag Chemical / Jiangsu Zhongqi Technology (中旗股份, SZSE ChiNext 300575), Nanjing
profile: Zhang Ji (b. 1978) co-founded Nanjing Flag Chemical in 2001-02 and is, with chairman Wu Yaojun, a joint actual controller of Jiangsu Zhongqi (Flagchem), a Nanjing pesticide maker founded in 2003 and listed on ChiNext in December 2016. She has been a company director since 2012 and holds about 5.6% directly. The firm makes herbicides, insecticides and fungicides and is expanding into pharma and new materials.
interesting_fact: Flagchem focuses on 'green', high-efficiency low-toxicity crop protection chemicals, with production bases in Nanjing, Huai'an and a new site in Huaibei, Anhui.
deep_cut_fact: A Nanjing University literature graduate, she began her career as a clerk at Shanghai Foreign Economic and Trade International Freight (1999-2001) before helping set up Nanjing Flag Chemical in 2001-02, where she served as director and manager until 2014.
notes: Company also lists marketing@flagchem.com. Board secretary is Lu Yang (per 10jqka) - IR route via annual report on cninfo. Low public profile.
